+---
+authors: Parmpreet Singh (parmjassal.singh@gmail.com)
+state: draft
+---
+
+
+# RFD 1 - Remote Job Worker
+
+## Required Approvers
+
+- Engineering: Any 2 approvals from this list ( `nklaassen` `marcoandredinis` `russjones` `zmb3` `rosstimothy` `r0mant` )
+
+
+## What
+This document gives an overview of the worker which can run commands on a host initiated by authorized remote user.
+
+
+## Why
+There are protocols like `SSH`, `NinjaOne`,  which allow remote users to execute commands on a host. But lacks in features as below
+  - Provide authentication which requires manual setup of the keys.
+  - Unable to differentiate `roles` associated with `user` while executing commands.
+  - `SSH` also doesn't provide a mechanism to fire and forget commands, and needs dependency on other tools to not break the connection.
+
+
+## Details
+
+- The **job worker service** is going to provide APIs in order to ease the process for remote execution of commands
+
+  - start
+  - stop
+  - status
+  - stream
+
+- The command to start the job service `remote-job-worker --work-directory=<> --port=<> [--bind-ip=<0.0.0.0>] [--certificate=<>] [--truststore=<>] [--key=<>]`. [if truststore is not provided, system truststore will be used as fallaback]
+
+- It provides a **client-side tool** that the user will use to invoke these APIs. (For this assignment only single remote host is targetted)
+  - start:
+    - Command: `rjwctl job start --host=<> --port=<> [--certificate=<>] [--truststore=<>] [--key=<>] COMMAND` like `rjwctl job start --host=127.0.0.1 --port=100 ls -a -l /home`
+    - Output: `Job with id <> is triggered`
+    - Example: `bin/rjexec start --host="127.0.0.1" --port=510051 --certificate=<> --key=<> --truststore=<> -- ls -al`
+  - stop:
+    - Command: `rjwctl job stop --host=<> --port=<> [--force] [--certificate=<>] [--truststore=<>] [--key=<>] <job-id>`
+    - Output: `Stop is triggered for Job with id <>`
+  - status:
+    - Command: `rjwctl job status --host=<> --port=<> [--certificate=<>] [--truststore=<>] [--key=<>] <job-id>`
+    - Output:
+```
+JobID: <>
+Status: RUNNING | FAILED | STOPPED | SUCCESS
+StartTime: <>
+Duration: <> // Currently in ms
+StartedBy: <>
+StoppedBy: <> // Only available if stopped using API
+ExitCode: <>  // Only populated in all cases except when stopped by.
+```
+  - stream:
+    - Command: `rjwctl job stream --host=<> --port=<> [--certificate=<>] [--trustore=<>] <job-id>`
+    - Output: Same as bytes emitted as stdout/stderr by the command remotely. Except for some commands that directly update the buffer like top.
+
+### Protocol Definitions
+
+ 
+ ```.proto
+
+message JobStartRequest {
+    string command = 1;
+    repeated string args = 2;
+    // Num of required millicores
+    int32 cpu_limit = 3;
+    // Memory required, it can be expressed as 1000MB or 1GB
+    string memory_limit = 4;
+    // Disk IO required, it can be expressed as 1MB/s or 2MB/s.
+    // Read and Write will have separate limits
+    string disk_read_io_limit = 5;
+    string disk_write_io_limit = 6;
+}
+
+message JobStartResponse {
+    // JobID which can be used for status check
+    string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message JobStatusRequest {
+    string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+// Will rely on error code from grpc for resource not found
+message JobStatusResponse {
+    enum Status {
+        RUNNING = 0;
+        FAILED = 1;
+        COMPLETED = 2;
+        STOPPED = 3;
+    }
+
+    Status status = 1;
+    // Useful for debugging in case of Failures.
+    string message = 2;
+    int32 start_time_ms = 3;
+    int32 duration_ms = 4;
+    // Identity of the remote user's
+    string started_by = 5;
+    string stopped_by = 6;
+    int32 exit_code = 7;
+}
+
+message JobStopRequest {
+    string job_id = 1;
+    bool force_stop = 2;
+}
+
+// Just a placeholder response. We can rely on the grpc code for operation status.
+message JobStopResponse {}
+
+message JobStreamRequest {
+    string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message JobStreamResponse {
+    bytes stream = 1;
+}
+
+service JobService {
+  rpc StartJob(JobStartRequest) returns (JobStartReponse);
+  rpc StopJob(JobStopRequest) returns (JobStopResponse);
+  rpc StatusJob(JobStatusRequest) returns (JobStatusResponse);
+  rpc StreamJobOutput(JobStreamRequest) return (stream JobStreamResponse);
+}
+
+```
+
+### Job Starting and saving associated job metadata
+
+
+```mermaid
+graph LR
+        A[USER] -->|1 StartJob|B(Server Process)
+        B -->|2 Self Spawn using exec| C(3 Dummy/Pause process that will apply limits to self using cgroups)
+        C -->|4 Run User Command using exec| D(Process executing user command)
+```
+
+#### Steps involved in starting a job
+- Once the request is received by the server. The server will generate the ID using `uuid` package.
+- Server will self-spawn with --mode=`pause` (pause mode doesn't spawn grpc) to act as parent for user command and to apply cgroup limits beforehand. Server will
+  - pass the command as arguments and resource limit as flags like `remote-job-worker --mode=pause --cpu=<> --memory=<> --io-read=<> --io-write=<> cmd`
+  - map `pid` of the child `pause/dummy` process and will also keep the status of the process in memory.
+  - starting writing child's output stream `work-directory/<job-id>/logs`
+- Self-spawned process will run the user command using exec and put the child pid to `process group`. So it can handle the SIGKILL and pass it to all the descendants.
+- Self-spawned process will short-circuit its child output/err stream to its output stream.  Short-circuiting stream to parent because io for writing to log shouldn't be accounted towards limits from the user process limits.
+
+In memory struct
+```
+JobID: <>
+Status: RUNNING | FAILED | STOPPED | SUCCESS // Byte can be used here
+StartTime: <>
+Duration: <> // Currently in ms
+StartedBy: <>
+ExitCode: <> 
+```
+
+ #### Steps involved in stopping job
+
+ - Once the request lands on the server for stopping job-id.
+ - The server will find the pid for the corresponding job.
+ - Then it will issue SIGKIL using `syscall.kill`
+
+ #### Steps involved in streaming job
+ - Server receives the request to stream job-id.
+ - Server will find the logs to stream and start writing to the stream.
+ - The state where we are in the file will be kept in the closure of the go routine along with `grpc stream` object and the stream handler method will wait for notification from go routine about completion. If we reach `EOF`, we need to check the status of the process before reading again (it can create a hot io loop for the process which is not producing output, we can use Linux notification using syscall ionotify when EOF is reached and process is still running to prevent the io loop)
+
+  #### Steps involved in checking the status job  
+ - Server receives the request to check the status of job-id.
+ - Server will read the status from in memory and return it to the user.
+   
+
+### Security
+
+We are going to use encryption tls 1.3 for on-wire communication. TLS 1.3 provides more secure cipher suites than tls 1.2. We can control the communication to use tls 1.3 as both client and server are shipped by us.  TLS1.3 uses ephemeral keys by default for key exchange providing more security.
+
+We are going to use signed **X.509 certificates** from CA. The CA can be self-hosted as well but should be
+available in truststore for both the client and server. I will refer X.509 certificate  as a certificate throughout the document.
+
+#### Steps used for generating the certificate (Actual commands can be added in README.md)
+
+1) Update custom extension info in OpenSSL config and use this config for certificate generation. Enable copy extension as well.
+2) Generate a private key for CA using rsa with key size 4096
+3) Generate the certificate for CA using sha256.
+4) Move the CA certificate to the system trust store for both the client and server.
+5) Now generate the private keys for the server and client separately with RSA and a key size of 4096.
+6) Generate the CSR for the server using the key with CN as `remoteJobWorker` and SAN with the appropriate DNS and IP address of the server.
+7) Generate the server certificate by using the CA key
+8) Generate the CSR for the client using the  key with CN as `username` and SAN with the appropriate DNS and IP address of the client along with a custom extension having the right role.
+9) Generate the client certificate by using the CA key
+
+How cert will look like
+```
+X509v3 extensions:
+  X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
+    DNS:local, DNS:Shruthis-MacBook-Air.local, IP Address:127.0.0.1
+    1.2.3.4.5.6.7.8:
+        ..JobExecuteRead
+  X509v3 Subject Key Identifier:
+```

+1) Update custom extension info in OpenSSL config and use this config for certificate generation. Enable copy extension as well.
+2) Generate a private key for CA using rsa with key size 4096
+3) Generate the certificate for CA using sha256.
+4) Move the CA certificate to the system trust store for both the client and server.
+5) Now generate the private keys for the server and client separately with RSA and a key size of 4096.
+6) Generate the CSR for the server using the key with CN as `remoteJobWorker` and SAN with the appropriate DNS and IP address of the server.
+7) Generate the server certificate by using the CA key
+8) Generate the CSR for the client using the  key with CN as `username` and SAN with the appropriate DNS and IP address of the client along with a custom extension having the right role.
+9) Generate the client certificate by using the CA key
+
+How cert will look like
+```
+X509v3 extensions:
+  X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
+    DNS:local, DNS:Shruthis-MacBook-Air.local, IP Address:127.0.0.1
+    1.2.3.4.5.6.7.8:
+        ..JobExecuteRead
+  X509v3 Subject Key Identifier:
+```
+

+#### Authentication
+
+We will rely on the mTLS for identity validation. In production, the certificates presented by the server and client will be short-lived to reduce security issues for stale certificates. These certificates will be generated through automation and delivered through agents, but in this assignment, they will be manually generated and signed by the CA.
+
+In practice, the certificate will contain the below attributes.
+- CN will contain the username or the device ID.
+- SAN will contain DNS or IP address.
+Apart from the authenticity of the certificate which will be done by default, we can use SAN to validate whether the peer of the connection is the same as in SAN.
+
+There are other mechanisms to authenticate like the secret key to sign the request and then use the passed signature and access key to validate the caller by invoking identity management like how it is done with/in AWS services. It adds an external dependency.
+

+
+```

+Error : rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc =
+"transport: authentication handshake failed: tls: failed to verify
+certificate: x509: certificate is valid for 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, not
+192.168.0.179"%
+```
+
+#### Authorization
+
+We will use the extension from the certificate to embed the roles.  We can use the below roles for this assignment:-
+(User below refers to CN from the certificate, for assignment will target actual human users instead of devices.)
+
+- `JobExecuteRead`: The user can start/stop/status/stream it's job.
+- `JobGlobalRead`: The user can status/stream everyone's job.
